answer: Sybil resistance rests on a stake bond held in a shared registry vault. Each agent identity must lock a minimum amount before acting, bound to a unique slot, so duplicates cannot claim the same work. Payouts settle through that same vault ledger, so a clone must post the full bond again, and proven duplication slashes it. A periodic pulse reconciles the ledger each window, stripping bonds from identities lacking distinct history. Legitimacy is a proven pigment of cost: to field N identities an attacker pays N times the bond while payoff does not scale, making the attack loss-making.
